epithet: The hypocrites, in their own words
lede: A boy overheard the most powerful man in Madinah say two things he should not have. He reported them, was disbelieved, and went home crushed. Then this surah came down and repeated both sentences word for word.

names.name: al-Munāfiqūn
names.note: After those it describes, from its first ayah. The Prophet ﷺ recited it, by this name, in the second unit of the Friday prayer (Muslim 877).

revelation.detail: It is Madinan without disagreement, and the commentators agree that it came down about ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy and those like him. Its occasion is narrated in the two Ṣaḥīḥs by the man it vindicated, and falls on the return from the expedition against the Banū al-Muṣṭaliq, at the watering-place of al-Muraysīʿ — in the fifth or sixth year.
revelation.when: Madinah, on the return from the expedition of al-Muraysīʿ — the fifth or sixth year of the Hijrah

evidence.quote: وَهِيَ مَدَنِيَّةٌ بِإجْماعِهِمْ وَذَكَرَ أهْلُ التَّفْسِيرِ أنَّها نَزَلَتْ في عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أُبَيٍّ ونُظَرائِهِ
سُورَةُ الْمُنَافِقُونَ مَدَنِيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ الْجَمِيعِ، وَهِيَ إِحْدَى عَشْرَةَ آيَةً

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ، والنَّحّاسُ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهْ، والبَيْهَقِيُّ في «الدَّلائِلِ»، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ «المُنافِقِينَ» بِالمَدِينَةِ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Madinah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, al-Naḥḥās, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.

setting: Before the Hijrah, the people of Yathrib had been about to crown ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy their king. The arrival of the Prophet ﷺ ended that, and he never forgave it. He professed Islam after Badr, when it had become the prudent thing to do, and spent the rest of his life working against it from inside.

On the way back from al-Muraysīʿ a quarrel broke out at the well between a hired man of the Emigrants and an ally of the Helpers; each called on his own side, and for a moment the old tribal cry was raised. Ibn Ubayy saw his chance. Zayd ibn Arqam, then a boy, tells it: “I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy say: ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah, until they break away from him.’ And: ‘If we return to Madinah, the mightier will surely drive out the meaner.’ I told my uncle, and he told the Prophet ﷺ.”

Ibn Ubayy was sent for. He swore he had said nothing of the kind, and men of his tribe spoke up for him: the boy must have misheard. “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ believed him and disbelieved me,” Zayd says, “and a grief came over me such as I had never known. I stayed in my house.” Then the surah was sent down. “The Prophet ﷺ sent for me and recited it, and said: Allah has confirmed you, Zayd.”

Ibn Ubayy’s own son, a sincere believer, stood at the gate of Madinah with his sword drawn and would not let his father enter until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave leave — so that he would know which of the two was the mightier.

occasions.title: What Zayd ibn Arqam heard
occasions.text: Zayd ibn Arqam said: “I was on a campaign and heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy say: ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah, until they disperse from around him; and if we return, the mightier will drive out the meaner from it.’ I mentioned it to my uncle, and he mentioned it to the Prophet ﷺ, who called me, and I told him. He sent for ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy and his companions, and they swore they had not said it. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disbelieved me and believed him, and a grief came over me such as had never come over me before. I sat at home, and my uncle said: ‘What did you want, but that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ should call you a liar and detest you?’ Then Allah sent down: ‘When the hypocrites come to you.’ The Prophet ﷺ sent for me and recited it, and said: ‘Allah has confirmed you, Zayd.’”
story: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh tells what had set it off. They were on a campaign when a man of the Emigrants struck a man of the Helpers from behind. The Helper cried, “Help, Helpers!” and the Emigrant, “Help, Emigrants!” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard it and said: “What is this cry of the days of ignorance?” They told him what had happened. He said: “Leave it; it is a foul thing.”

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy heard of it and said: “So they have done it? By Allah, if we return to Madinah, the mightier will drive out the meaner from it.” It reached the Prophet ﷺ, and ʿUmar stood up: “Messenger of Allah, let me strike the neck of this hypocrite.” He ﷺ said: “Leave him. Let people not say that Muḥammad kills his companions.”
occasions.source: Zayd ibn Arqam: al-Bukhārī (4900) and Muslim (2772). Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh: al-Bukhārī (4905) and Muslim (2584).

aim: To expose the hypocrites, their traits and their stance towards Islam and its people — as a warning against them, and against resembling them.
themes: Wealth and children as a distraction

outline.title: What they are
outline.summary: When the hypocrites come to you they say, “We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah.” Allah knows that you are His Messenger — and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars. They have made their oaths a cover. They believed and then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed. When you see them, their appearance pleases you, and when they speak you listen; but they are like timbers propped against a wall. They think every cry is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them.

outline.title: Too proud to be forgiven
outline.summary: When it is said to them, “Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you,” they turn their heads aside in arrogance. It is the same whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not: Allah will not forgive them.

outline.title: The two sentences
outline.summary: They are the ones who say, “Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah, until they disperse” — when to Allah belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth. They say, “If we return to Madinah, the mightier will drive out the meaner” — when might belongs to Allah, to His Messenger and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know.

outline.title: To the believers
outline.summary: O you who believe, do not let your wealth and your children distract you from the remembrance of Allah. Spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you and he says, “My Lord, if only You would grant me a little more time, so that I might give in charity and be among the righteous.” Allah does not delay a soul when its term has come.

keyAyah.why: The answer to Ibn Ubayy’s boast, and the Qurʾan’s statement of where honour comes from.

virtues.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in the Friday prayer Sūrat al-Jumuʿah and “When the hypocrites come to you”.

before: Al-Jumuʿah reproached people who left the Prophet ﷺ standing for a caravan. Al-Munāfiqūn describes people who stayed, and swore, and lied.
after: This surah ends by warning that wealth and children can distract from Allah. Al-Taghābun says it more sharply: they are a trial — and the Day when the loss is counted has a name.
